question: Refer to the exhibit. What is the result of this series of commands?
context:
UCS-A# scope adapter 1/1/1
UCS-A /chassis/server/adapter # show image
Name                         Type      Version    State
---------------------------  --------  ---------  --------
ucs-m81kr-vic.2.2.1b.bin     Adapter   2.2(1b)    Active

UCS-A /chassis/server/adapter # update firmware 2.2(1b)
UCS-A /chassis/server/adapter* # activate firmware 2.2(1b) set-startup-only
UCS-A /chassis/server/adapter* # commit-buffer
UCS-A /chassis/server/adapter #
options: It activates the firmware on the next adapter boot.
It updates the firmware on adapter 1/1/1 immediately.
It verifies the firmware update on the server.
theory: In the UCS CLI, 'update firmware' copies (downloads) a new firmware image to an endpoint, while a separate 'activate firmware ... set-startup-only' step only changes the startup version pointer without immediately switching the running image. The 'set-startup-only' keyword specifically defers activation: the new firmware becomes active only the next time the adapter (or endpoint) reboots, rather than forcing an immediate reboot or activation. This two-step update/activate model lets administrators stage firmware changes and control exactly when disruption occurs. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Firmware Updates, Direct Firmware Update)
